name: Student Residence Permit

requirements.blocker_text: This requires admission from a recognised institution.
requirements.fix_path: Secure admission from a recognised institution.

value.note: practical minimum cited by universities; not a single federal statutory figure

requirements.blocker_text: This requires proof of funds (commonly cited around CHF 21,000/year), mandatory health/accident insurance, and adequate accommodation. Must declare intent to leave after studies.

evidence_required.document: Proof of funds and health/accident insurance

sources.title: Residence for study purposes - State Secretariat for Migration

notes: SOURCING CAVEAT flagged honestly: the CHF 21,000/year funds figure is a widely-cited practical minimum from university admissions guidance, not a single codified federal statutory figure the way several other countries' student-funds thresholds are in this dataset. Non-EU/EFTA students must wait 6 months after arrival before working, then max 15 hours/week during term, up to 100% during breaks (employer needs a separate work permit) — EU/EFTA students may work from day one, a genuine two-tier distinction consistent with the rest of Switzerland's system. GENUINE, DISTINCTIVE POST-STUDY PROVISION: non-EU graduates of recognised Swiss institutions may apply for a 6-month, non-renewable job-search permit, and the Inländervorrang labour-market test can be WAIVED for graduate hires where the job is of high scientific or economic interest (Art. 21(3) FNIA) — with ETH/EPFL and Swiss university graduates receiving preferential treatment, a real and confirmed structural advantage worth flagging as a bridge into ch_third_country_work_permit.
